title: There Is a God — All Nature Speaks
description: There Is a God — All Nature Speaks in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 101 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Being of God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: There is a God all na-ture speaks, Through earth, and air, and sea, and skies: See, from the clouds his glo-ry breaks, When first the beams of morn-ing rise.

lines: There is a God — all nature speaks,
Through earth, and air, and sea, and skies:
See, from the clouds his glory breaks,
When first the beams of morning rise.
O'er the wide world's extended frame
The flowery tribes, all blooming, rise
Above the weak attempts of art;
Speak sweet conviction to the heart.
Ye curious minds, who roam abroad,
Confess the footsteps of a God;
Come, bow before him, and adore.

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
